pairs.question: Nihilne te, Materne, fabulae malignorum terrent, quo minus offensas Catonis tui ames? An ideo librum istum adprehendisti, ut diligentius retractares, et sublatis si qua pravae interpretationi materiam dederunt, emitteres Catonem non quidem meliorem, sed tamen securiorem?
pairs.answer: Leges quid Maternus sibi debuerit, et adgnosces quae audisti.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange: Secundus asks Maternus whether the gossip frightens him and whether he took up the book to revise it. Dropped framing 'inquit' in both utterances; kept the vocative 'Materne' as part of the question. Answer stops at the first full stop ('audisti'); the continuation ('Quod si qua omisit Cato, sequenti recitatione Thyestes dicet...') turns from answering to discussing his Thyestes plans, so it is cut.

pairs.question: Num parum tempestivus interveni secretum consilium et causae alicuius meditationem tractantibus?
pairs.answer: Minime, minime, atque adeo vellem maturius intervenisses.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange: Messalla, entering, asks whether he has come at a bad time. Dropped framing 'inquit' from question and from Secundus's reply. Answer stops at the first full stop ('intervenisses'); what follows ('delectasset enim te et Apri nostri accuratissimus sermo...') elaborates on what he missed rather than answering, so it is cut.
